reader.requirement: At 1985 (level 2), under dynamic access one open file may be read randomly (format 2) and sequentially (format 1 with NEXT, which 1985 requires), written in any key order, and positioned by START, the sequential reads continuing from the record a random READ or START established.

edition-consulted.switches: at 1985 a dynamic-access sequential READ must write NEXT (COBOL7144); 2002 on implies it
whether a random READ of an alternate key whose next record has the same value answers 02 (1985) or 00 (2002 on)

reader.notes: The connector branches only on KeyedAccess.Dynamic per statement form; the 1985-specific parts (mandatory NEXT, no PREVIOUS) are compile-time arms that take the 1985 branch.

refuter.evidence: Probe rb_dyn.cob (run rb_dyn-002), DYNAMIC access: READ NEXT AA, then WRITE BB (ahead of the position), then READ NEXT gave BB (OK §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR5 'The file position indicator is not affected by the execution of a WRITE statement', with IX.4.5.4 GR4d). DELETE current, then NEXT gave CC (OK §1985:IX.4.3.4 GR6). Random READ KEY IS IX-ALT m3, then REWRITE moving the alternate key to m6, then NEXT gave EEm5 and then CCm6 again, as a key-value position requires (OK §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR7). A random READ on the duplicates key gave 02 AA; NEXT gave 02 CC, 00 GG, 00 EE, which is IX.4.5.4 GR4e. A random READ by prime EE re-established the prime as key of reference, and NEXT gave GG. Probes rb_dyn-001 and rf_acc confirm the 1985 refusals the reader did not try: COBOL6826 for WRITE with no INVALID KEY and no USE, and 'ALTERNATE KEY' with no RECORD refused. OK §1985:IX.2.4.4 GR4.
